source.wording_notes:
About the source: the URL above is the official video. It is on the Toastmasters International YouTube channel under the title "2015 World Champion of Public Speaking - Mohammed Qahtani" (checked through YouTube oEmbed), and the Toastmasters press release links to it ("Watch Qahtani compete"). YouTube blocked the caption download, so I could not check the clip against the official audio. I checked it against two independent transcripts that agree closely: Speakola (speakola.com/other-events/mohammed-qahtani-toastmasters-power-of-words-2015) and English Speeches Channel (library.englishspeecheschannel.com/speech/mohammed-qahtani-power-of-words). These clip.md lines differ from both transcripts:
(1) Line 11: clip says "three times as many AS people dying from smoking". Both transcripts say "three times as many people dying from smoking", with no second "as".
(2) Line 11: clip says "Snickers bar". Both transcripts say "Snicker bar". English Speeches has "pulled", which matches the clip; Speakola has "put".
(3) Line 13: clip says "nothing WILL ever happen to you". Both transcripts say "nothing WOULD ever happen to you".
(4) Line 16: clip says "I USED these arguments". Both transcripts say "I USE these arguments", which is how he says it on stage.
(5) Line 12: the first word is unverified. The clip has "Oh, you all think smoking kills?", Speakola has "Or you all think...", and English Speeches has "All you all think... Yes."
(6) Beat B7 is a template, not the transcript, but it drops "just". The original is "even though I JUST made them up".
Lines 14 (DNA), 16 (tobacco farming), 15 ("Mr. Contest Chair, fellow Toastmasters and guests"), 17 ("five of them believed what I said, two of them started smoking") and 18 ("Words, when said and articulated in the right way, can change someone's mind.") match the transcripts word for word.
The stage directions are unverified: patting his pockets for a lighter, then dropping the act and opening his arms. Speakola only notes "[Pretending to light up a cigarette]".
The clip stops at "change someone's mind". The next line in the original is "They can alter someone's belief."

claims_false.claim: The number of people dying from diabetes is three times the number dying from smoking
claims_false.status: false (it is the other way round). Worldwide, tobacco kills more than 7 million people a year, against 1.6 million deaths directly caused by diabetes in 2021, so roughly 4 times more. In the US, cigarette smoking and secondhand smoke cause more than 480,000 deaths a year, against 94,445 diabetes deaths in 2024, so roughly 5 times more.
claims_false.source: WHO Tobacco and nicotine fact sheet, 26 Jun 2026 (who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/tobacco); WHO Diabetes fact sheet, 14 Nov 2024 (who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/diabetes); CDC About Commercial Tobacco (cdc.gov/tobacco/about/index.html); CDC FastStats Diabetes (cdc.gov/nchs/fastats/diabetes.htm)

claims_false.claim: The leading cause of lung cancer is not cigarettes, it is your DNA
claims_false.status: false. CDC: 'Cigarette smoking is the number one risk factor for lung cancer', and in the US it is 'linked to about 80% of lung cancer deaths'. WHO: 'Smoking tobacco ... is the primary risk factor for lung cancer', and most preventable cases are attributable to tobacco smoking (60-70%). WHO lists 'genetic susceptibility' only as one of several secondary risk factors.
claims_false.source: CDC Lung Cancer Risk Factors (cdc.gov/lung-cancer/risk-factors/index.html, May 2026); WHO Lung cancer fact sheet, 16 Apr 2026 (who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/lung-cancer)

claims_false.claim: You could smoke for years and nothing will ever happen to you
claims_false.status: false or misleading (a survivor anecdote). WHO: tobacco 'damages nearly every organ in the body' and 'there is no safe level of exposure'. CDC: cigarette smoking 'harms nearly every organ of the body'.
claims_false.source: WHO Tobacco and nicotine fact sheet, 26 Jun 2026; CDC About Commercial Tobacco (cdc.gov/tobacco/about/index.html)

claims_false.claim: The whole war against smoking is just to restrict the farming of tobacco
claims_false.status: false. Article 3 of the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) states the treaty's goal as protecting 'present and future generations from the devastating health, social, environmental and economic consequences of tobacco consumption and exposure to tobacco smoke'. Article 17 requires countries to promote 'economically viable alternatives for tobacco workers, growers', and Article 4 includes providing assistance for tobacco workers and growers. Farmers are supported, not targeted.

claims_false.claim: He says himself that he made these arguments up
claims_false.status: confirmed. Both transcripts read 'I use these arguments — even though I just made them up — with a group of my friends'.
claims_false.source: Speakola transcript; English Speeches Channel transcript (both listed in wording_notes)

beats.skeleton: Silent for 2 to 3 seconds. Use a real prop to do the one thing a [your role] should never do. Then say one word that dares the viewer to judge you ('Yes?').
beats.spoken: [silent 3 s: he rolls up the mat that faces the camera, tucks it under his arm, sips his tea, looks into the lens] Yes?
beats.on_screen: Too stiff? Too old? 4 lies first. Then the truth.

beats.skeleton: [The kind thing everybody says]? Hmm. No no. Then turn it on the viewer in 3 words ('Not for you.').
beats.spoken: Yoga is for everybody? Hmm. No no. Not for you.
beats.on_screen: The voice in your head. Not me.

beats.skeleton: Lie 1, a false comparison with an everyday thing nobody questions: 'You can't [skill], you don't go to [class for that skill], right? Same same. Can't [body thing]? No [practice].'
beats.spoken: You can't cook... you don't go to cooking class, right? Same same. Can't touch your toes? No yoga.
beats.on_screen: LIE 1/4: 'Can't touch your toes? No yoga.'
beats.truth_source: Checked false: myths_data.py B_GROUPS id 'flexstart' (verified.json kept #57). Truth is given in B7 and B9: Yoga Sutra 2.46, tr. J. H. Woods 1914, 'Stable-and-easy posture'. Toes are not mentioned, so the truth says 'Nothing about toes', never 'no toes'.

beats.skeleton: Lie 2, the false cause: 'And the real reason? Not because [the thing you could change]. [A wrong reason nobody can change]. After [age]... finish.'
beats.spoken: And the real reason? Not because you never try. Your age. After forty... finish.
beats.on_screen: LIE 2/4: 'After forty, yoga is finished.'
beats.truth_source: Checked false: id 'young' (verified.json #35 + Yoga Mala sec. 39, ym.txt). Pattabhi Jois, Yoga Mala, sec. 39 Shirshasana (tr. Eddie Stern), on the claim that yoga should stop after forty: 'This is not borne out by experience...' and '...there is no age restriction for the practice of yoga.' Never quote the sentences around them ('the Science of yoga for the cure of diseases', 'suffering from a disease... can attain perfection'): those are medical claims. The 'except those who are lazy' line is also in ym.txt sec. 39 but is cut from this Reel.

beats.skeleton: Lie 3, the fixed-forever line: 'After [age]? [X] is [X]. [It is already decided]. Too late.'
beats.spoken: After sixty? Stiff is stiff. Your body already decide. Too late.
beats.on_screen: LIE 3/4: 'After sixty, stiff for life.'
beats.truth_source: Checked false: id 'flex60' (verified.json #55). Sivaramakrishnan et al., Int J Behav Nutr Phys Act 2019;16:33: a review of 22 trials, average age 60 or more (only 17 of the 22 measured physical function). Compared with no exercise, yoga improved lower-body flexibility, balance and leg strength. The gains were moderate, not miracles.

beats.skeleton: Lie 4, the hidden motive: 'And [practice]? Just [small thing]. [The viewer's own put-down]. They say "[the true benefit]"... just to sell you [product].' The motive pokes at the business, never at the practice.
beats.spoken: And yoga? Just stretching. Not real exercise. They say "yoga make you strong"... just to sell you yoga pants.
beats.on_screen: LIE 4/4: 'Yoga is just stretching.'
beats.truth_source: Checked false: id 'stretching' (verified.json #58). Tran et al., Prev Cardiol 2001;4(4):165: 10 untrained young adults (18-27) did hatha yoga at least twice a week for 8 weeks. Elbow strength rose 31% and knee-muscle endurance 57%. The study was small and had no control group. The 'yoga pants' motive is a joke at the yoga business, not a claim.

beats.skeleton: Drop the act. Put the prop down, use a softer voice and greet the viewer as yourself. Then say one line that names the voice they just heard. Then a 1 s silent beat before the truth.
beats.spoken: [puts the tea and the rolled mat down, softer voice] Okay. Stop. Hello, I'm Boonchu. You know that voice, right? [1 s silent beat: he looks at the rolled mat, then at the lens]
beats.on_screen: Lies over. Now the truth. Boonchu, teaching in Bangkok, 14 years.
beats.truth_source: 14 years teaching in Bangkok: Boonchu's confirmed shala years (plato.md standing order, 4 Oct 2026).

beats.skeleton: Confess in three words ('All four... wrong.'). Then one plain truth per lie, in the same order as the lies, each opened with the lie in the viewer's own words: '[Lie]? [Source, named so a beginner knows who] say [truth].'
beats.spoken: All four... wrong. Can't touch your toes? The old yoga book say: asana is stable and easy. Nothing about toes. After forty? Guruji... the teacher of my teacher... write in his book: no age limit. After sixty? A review of twenty-two trials, people sixty and up: with yoga, flexibility still improve. Not magic. But it move. Just stretching? Small study, young beginners... eight weeks of yoga, they get stronger.
beats.on_screen: 4 flip cards, one per truth: TRUE 1/4: Touch your toes? Not needed to start. / TRUE 2/4: No age limit (Guruji, Yoga Mala). / TRUE 3/4: After 60, flexibility still improves (moderate). / TRUE 4/4: Stronger in 8 weeks (small study).

Woods 1914: show only 'stable-and-easy' (verified.json #57). 2) Sri K. Pattabhi Jois (Guruji), Yoga Mala, sec. 39: '...there is no age restriction for the practice of yoga.' beats.skeleton: The result is about the viewer. Ask two questions, and make the second one cost more: 'How many you believe? And how many [years / mornings] they cost you?'
beats.spoken: So... how many you believe? And how many years... they cost you?
beats.on_screen: How many did you believe? How many years did they cost?
beats.truth_source: No result is claimed. It is a question to the viewer, with no invented counts.

beats.skeleton: Flip the B2 comparison into the truth and undo the B0 action: '[Class] is for people who can't [skill]. [Practice]... same same. [Our promise].'
beats.spoken: [unrolls the same mat toward the camera] Cooking class is for people who can't cook. Yoga... same same. We teach you from zero.

risks: The biggest risk is someone clipping the lie section (B1 to B5, about 25 s with his face). In the edit, the B0 card shrinks into a header pill, '4 LIES, THEN THE TRUTH · at 0:28', that stays burned in from 0 s until the 'Lies over' frame. The editor sets the time to the real frame. 'LIE n/4' is bigger than the myth quote on every lie line, and each myth gets a red strike-through when its line ends. All of this is burned in inside the safe area, not added as IG stickers, so a crop or re-upload keeps it. The cover and preview frame come only from B6 or B9. Never post B1 to B5 alone as a Story or teaser.

All 4 lies are real popular myths checked false in myths_data.py (flexstart, young, flex60, stretching). All are very low harm if clipped: they mostly keep someone at home. The one body risk: someone who believes 'just stretching' may walk into a vigorous class unprepared. The stretching entry has Mody 2011: 90% of predicted max heart rate by round 4 of Sun Salutation, in 6 trained young people. The caption's 'Tell your teacher before class' line covers it.

'After 50, no upside down' was dropped on purpose. With that myth the truth is the dangerous half: headstand doubled eye pressure, and NCCIH still says older adults may need to be cautious. A clipped truth line could lead someone with glaucoma to skip the eye doctor. Keep it for a separate, careful piece.
There is no invented number in B2. The clip's 'three times' comparison became a false comparison (the cooking class), because a made-up number would be a new false claim.

The science is modest. The 2019 review found moderate gains, and only 17 of its 22 trials measured physical function. 'People sixty and up' in B7 is a spoken shortcut: the trials had an average age of 60 or more, so the card says 'average age 60+'. The strength study had 10 untrained young adults (18-27) and no control group, and the 31% is elbow strength only. Say 'small study, young beginners'. Never say 'Ashtanga reverses ageing'.

Exact wording matters. Woods 1914: show only 'stable-and-easy'. 'Posture' breaks the asana rule, and 'steady and comfortable' is not confirmed. Quote Yoga Mala word for word, with the ellipsis: '...there is no age restriction for the practice of yoga.' and 'This is not borne out by experience...'. Never quote the sentences around them (cure of diseases, 'can attain perfection'). The caption's 'wrote that there is no age limit' is also word for word: a later Yoga Mala section has 'There is no age limit for the practice of yoga' (ym.txt). No Guruji or Sharath photo.

B5 targets the yoga business, which is a fair target. 'They say' marks the quote by ear. Clipped without the LIE 4/4 tag, though, the line could still look like Boonchu dismissing yoga. The tag must sit on that line.
'After forty' and 'after sixty' are said only in the lie voice and are labelled as lies. Never call a person old on screen, and no student appears in frame.

Length is about 60 to 62 s at 1.3x with the pauses cut: B0 0-3 s, lies 3-29 s, 'Lies over' at about 29 s, B6 plus the 1 s beat 29-33 s, truths 33-52 s, B8 52-56 s, B9 56-61 s. The speaker's own phrases were avoided: no 'Oh, you think' opener, no 'Let me tell you something', no 'What?' (it is 'Yes?' here), no Snickers, no 'for years and nothing will happen', no contest greeting, no 'Five of them believed', no 'said in the right way', no 'war against'. Only the shape and rhythm are kept.
'How many years did they cost you?' in B8 is a sharp line for an open-door Reel. B9's warm close and the mat unrolling must follow at once.

B8 stays a question. If Boonchu insists on a real count, the line must name who was asked and use only the count he reports: 'I tried it on 2 of my team. [Boonchu's real count] believed.' Never write a beginner count, and never film it before he gives the number.

The English caption is 6 lines, one more than the 5-line default. The extra line is the care line ('New to exercise or have an injury?'). Keep it. The Thai line 1 keeps 'แบบหน้าตาย' because it is natural Thai. Only the English idiom was the problem.

final.title: Spot the Four Lies

beats.skeleton: Silent, 2 to 3 s: do one odd, slightly 'wrong' thing with an everyday prop from the topic. Look into the lens. Say one word that dares the viewer to judge you. On screen from frame 1: the game banner and the viewer's own thought.
beats.spoken: (silent, 2 to 3 s: after practice he slowly wrings his soaked towel with both hands. Drops fall beside the mat. He looks up at the lens, one eyebrow up.) What?
beats.on_screen: SPOT THE LIES 0/4 · You think: "It's just sweat."

beats.skeleton: Say the viewer's own thought back as a 2-word question. Laugh it off. Take the floor in 2 or 3 words.
beats.spoken: (big, confident yoga-salesman voice from here to the end of B5) Just sweat? (laughs) No no no. Sit. I explain.
beats.on_screen: SPOT THE LIES 0/4

beats.skeleton: Lie 1, the comparison: 'The more you ___, the more ___.' Hold up an everyday object, or the viewer's own, as the 'proof'. No numbers inside a lie.
beats.spoken: More you sweat... more fat you burn. (lifts the wet towel to the lens) Your towel after practice? Fat. Melting.
beats.on_screen: SPOT THE LIES · LIE 1/4: "More sweat, more fat burned"
beats.truth_source: LIE, checked false: 'The more you sweat, the more fat you burn.' myths_data.py B_GROUPS id='sweatfat'; verified.json kept #51; Meerman and Brown, BMJ 2014;349:g7257 (UNSW Newsroom, 14 Mar 2018)

beats.skeleton: Lie 2, the false cause: 'You feel ___ after ___? Not the ___ (the plain cause). It's ___ (the magic cause).' Show the body part, then act it out with the prop.
beats.spoken: You feel fresh after Marichyasana D? Not the stretch. Your liver (touches his right ribs)... squeezed clean. (wrings the towel again) Like this towel.
beats.on_screen: SPOT THE LIES · LIE 2/4: "Twists squeeze your liver clean"
beats.truth_source: LIE, checked false: 'Twists squeeze toxins out of your organs like a wet towel.' myths_data.py id='twists'; verified.json kept #67 (Herpreet Thind, UMass Lowell, quoted by Shawn Radcliffe, Yoga Journal, 18 Jan 2022: 'no scientific basis') and #44 (Pam Peake, ACSM, CBS News, 15 Apr 2016). Aimed at the internet 'detox sponge' claim, never at Jois or the old texts (verified #44 safety). Asana: Marichyasana D, Primary

beats.skeleton: Lie 3, the safety promise: 'You ___ first? Good. Then you won't ___. Guaranteed.'
beats.spoken: You stretch first, before practice? Good. Then you won't get hurt. (one finger up) Guaranteed.
beats.on_screen: SPOT THE LIES · LIE 3/4: "Stretch first and you won't get hurt"
beats.truth_source: LIE, checked false: myths_data.py id='stretchfirst', title 'Stretch first and you won't get hurt', myth 'A quick stretch before exercise prevents injury.'; verified.json kept #54; Lauersen et al., Br J Sports Med 2014;48(11):871

beats.skeleton: Lie 4, the 'it's only' shrink, said with the most confidence: 'That ___ you hate? Relax. It's only ___.' Then show the 'proof' with your own body.
beats.spoken: (his most confident salesman voice) You hate the jump back? Relax. Yoga is only stretching. Your arms? (lets them hang loose) Just resting.
beats.on_screen: SPOT THE LIES · LIE 4/4: "Yoga is only stretching"
beats.truth_source: LIE, checked false: 'Yoga is only stretching.' myths_data.py id='stretching'; verified.json kept #58; Tran et al., Prev Cardiol 2001;4(4):165 (10 people, no control group); Mody, J Bodyw Mov Ther 2011;15(3):343 (6 trained people). Asana: Chaturanga Dandasana in Surya Namaskara A and B

beats.skeleton: Frame break: put the prop down, switch to your real voice, say the plain count of lies, smile, greet the real audience in 2 to 4 words.
beats.spoken: (drops the towel on the mat, sits easy, his normal teacher voice, small smile) Four lies. Okay... okay. Hello, my friends.
beats.on_screen: ALL 4 WERE LIES

beats.skeleton: Confession with the twist: 'But... none of them is mine.' Name where people hear them (online, gyms; never a named person, never teachers). One mirror line: 'You hear them too.'
beats.spoken: But... none of them is mine. You find them online... in gyms. You hear them too, no?
beats.on_screen: Not mine. Online, in gyms: you hear them too.
beats.truth_source: Popular claims, myths_data.py group 'What people believe about yoga and exercise'. Verified #44 and #67 safety notes: aim at the internet claim, never at teachers, Jois or the old texts.

beats.skeleton: 'The truth?' Then one plain true line per lie, in the same order, each from the checked file, each with its safety line. Then turn the count on the viewer: 'How many you believe? One? All ___?' Never invent anyone's results.
beats.spoken: The truth? (beat) Sweat is not fat. Fat go out mostly in your breath. Breathing faster... don't burn more. Twist? No proof it squeeze your liver clean. It help you turn. final.title: Old Book, Big Promises

beats.skeleton: Silent prop, about 2 s, started mid-action: do the small 'wrong' thing the room would judge (here: a yoga teacher checking his own face like a vain man). Then one short line that turns the judgment back on the viewer: 'Eh? You never ___?'
beats.spoken: (silent, 2 s) ... Eh? You never check?
beats.on_screen: GAME: 3 old promises. Which do you believe? | [SERIES: Boonchu to pick]

beats.skeleton: Name the viewer's quiet worry as a question, refuse it with full confidence, and set the game out loud: '___ for years... still ___? No no no. Listen... and count.'
beats.spoken: Years on the mat... still getting older? No no no. Listen... and count.
beats.on_screen: GAME: 3 promises from an old yoga book

beats.skeleton: Promise 1: the book's practice in two words + a number + what it takes away, then the mirror: '___. [number]... ___, gone. ___, gone. [number]! And you... still ___. One by one.'
beats.spoken: Upside down. Six months... wrinkles, gone. Grey hair, gone. Six months! And you... still pull it out. One by one.
beats.on_screen: GAME 1/3 · Old book: six months upside down, no grey hair. True?
beats.truth_source: Hatha Yoga Pradipika 3.80 to 3.81, tr. Pancham Sinh 1914: 'Place the head on the ground and the feet up into the sky...' and 'After six months, the wrinkles and grey hair are not seen.' Myth file myths_data.py B_GROUPS id 'grey'; verified.json 'Six months upside down'. The book means Viparita Karani (a mudra); nearest Ashtanga forms are Sirsasana and Sarvangasana. 'Head on the floor. Feet to the sky.' is cut from the speech: said with full confidence it is a how-to for going upside down (verified.json 'In headstand, the head just rests': the head carries 40 to 48% of body weight; 'No upside-down after 50': headstand doubled eye pressure). 'Conquers death' (same verse) left out on purpose.

beats.skeleton: Promise 2, the wrong cause: '___? No no. [the real cause, per the act]... [its plain name]. Even ___... become ___. ___ and ___... like ___ again.'
beats.spoken: Cream? No no. Mula Bandha... root lock. Even an old man... become young. Breath and bandha... like sixteen again.
beats.on_screen: GAME 2/3 · Old book: Mula Bandha makes an old man young. True?
beats.truth_source: HYP 3.64 (Sinh): 'Even an old man becomes young by constantly practising Mula Bandha.' The card follows this verse and gives no 16 to Mula Bandha. HYP 2.47 (Sinh): 'By pulling up the Apana Vayu and by forcing the Prana Vayu down the throat, the Yogi... becomes young, as it were 16 years old'; Muktibodhananda 2.47: 'appears as if sixteen years of age' (verified.json 'The old man who becomes sixteen'). The 16 comes from that breath practice, so the line says 'breath and bandha', and 'like sixteen' keeps the book's own hedge ('as it were', 'as if'). 'Root lock' is the plain meaning of Mula Bandha, said once so the name is explained the first time. Myth file id 'sixteen'.

beats.skeleton: Promise 3, the biggest one, as a wrong belief corrected with full confidence: '[asana]? Just ___? No no. The ___... ___. The worst ___.'
beats.spoken: Mayurasana? Just an arm balance? No no. The peacock... kill poison. The worst poison.
beats.on_screen: GAME 3/3 · Old book: the peacock asana (Mayurasana) kills poison. True?
beats.truth_source: HYP 1.33 in Sinh (1.31 in modern editions): Mayurasana 'destroys the most deadly poison' (Sanskrit 'jarayet kala-kutam', kalakuta), so 'kill poison' follows Sinh's 'destroys'. Myth file id 'peacock'; verified.json 'The peacock that digests the world's worst poison'. 'Big mistake' (not in the book, pushes viewers to do a strong belly-pressure asana) is cut. Left out of speech: 'destroys all diseases' and 'digests unwholesome food taken in excess' (could push someone to do it on a full stomach). Shiva and the kalakuta legend kept out of the act.

beats.skeleton: Drop the act after a 1 s silent beat: take off the prop, change to the normal voice, catch the viewer: 'Okay, okay. You almost believe me. ... None of this is mine.'
beats.spoken: (1 s silent: takes the reading glasses off, folds them, small smile at himself; then normal voice) Okay, okay. You almost believe me. ... None of this is mine.
beats.on_screen: GAME OVER. All 3: no proof.
beats.truth_source: 'No proof' sums up B8: the grey hair and poison promises have never been tested (myth file 'grey' f, 'peacock' f) and 'Nobody turns sixteen' (myth file 'sixteen' f).

beats.skeleton: Name the real source, then one mirror line: 'A [age] ___ say it. [name]. You want it ___... I know.'
beats.spoken: A 500-year-old yoga book say it. Hatha Yoga Pradipika. You want it true... I know.
beats.on_screen: Hatha Yoga Pradipika, over 500 years old.
beats.truth_source: Age: verified.json ('Ashtanga is only for the young') gives the 15th century as the standard dating for Svatmarama, so 'over 500 years' is safe. The praise line and 'With a teacher' moved to B9, with their safety card.

beats.skeleton: The count, then one plain truth per promise, then the one true thing: 'So... how many you believe? One? ... All [n]? ... I wish. ___? No study test it. ___? Nobody ___. ___? No study. Keep away from ___. But ___. That one is true.'
beats.spoken: So... how many you believe? One? ... All three? ... I wish. Upside down for grey hair, for wrinkles? No study test it. Sixteen again? Nobody turn sixteen. Poison? No study. Keep away from poison. But old muscle still answer training. That one is true.
beats.on_screen: ❌ Upside down for grey hair: never tested / ❌ Sixteen again: nobody / ❌ Poison: no study, then alone: ✅ Old muscle still answers training
beats.truth_source: 'I wish': Boonchu's own letter P.S. ('I wish we could say we are growing young', Plato notebook, LETTER FORMAT); 'Me too' is cut because nothing checked says he believed all three. Grey hair and wrinkles: myth file 'grey' f 'No study has tested the second' (the six-month line, which names wrinkles and grey hair); verified.json 'Six months upside down: no wrinkles, no grey hair': 'No study of inversions on hair or wrinkles exists' (another verifier hedged it as 'we found no study'). Grey hair itself HAS been studied (Rosenberg et al., eLife 2021), so the line and the card name the upside-down promise, never grey hair alone. Sixteen: myth file 'sixteen' f 'Nobody turns sixteen.' Poison: myth file 'peacock' f ('No study has tested this... Keep away from poison.'). The old 'Go to hospital' line is cut; its source was verified.json 'The peacock that digests the world's worst poison' safety ('real poisoning needs emergency care'), not the myth file. Old muscle: Robinson et al., Cell Metabolism 2017 (Mayo Clinic), ages 65 to 80, 12 weeks of interval training, muscle cell energy capacity +69% (myth file 'sixteen' f). That was cycling intervals, not yoga and not bandhas, so the spoken line says 'training' and no number is spoken. No result from Boonchu's friends or students is claimed.

beats.skeleton: The moral in one line, aimed at the promise and at Boonchu (never the book), then the book's gold with the teacher, the habit line, and the book's own last word: 'Big ___... so easy to ___. Even when I ___. But the book has gold too. ___. With a teacher. That part... we still do. And the book say: ___. Only ___.' (prop callback closes the B0 loop)
beats.spoken: Big promise... so easy to love. Even when I say it. But the book has gold too. One second the first day... a little more each day. With a teacher. That part... we still do. And the book say: from reading, no success. Only from practice. (turns the phone face down, puts the folded glasses on it, steps onto the mat)
beats.on_screen: Start with one second. Learn inversions with a teacher. → Not from reading. From practice. (Hatha Yoga Pradipika 1.67, tr. Sinh 1914)
beats.truth_source: Moral: Boonchu's own words, aimed at the promise and at himself ('Even when I say it'), not at the book or its author, and no longer an echo of the speech's closing line. Gold line: HYP 3.80 (Sinh) 'for a second only the first day, and increase this time daily'. 'With a teacher': HYP 3.78 to 3.79 (Sinh) say Viparita Karani is learnt from the guru (verified.json 'Six months upside down, goodbye grey hair' evidence); verified.json 'Six months upside down: no wrinkles, no grey hair' safety: 'Do not suggest long holds' and inversions 'are learned step by step with a teacher', hence the first card. Last line: HYP 1.67 (Sinh): success comes from practice; 'by merely reading books' on yoga one never gets success. Confirmed in verified.json ('Too old after forty' evidence: 'Sinh 67 and 68 are by merely reading books and particular dress (Vesa), both confirmed'; 'Ashtanga is only for the young' evidence: 'The next verse says success comes only from practice, not from reading books'). Verse numbers differ by edition (on sacred-texts the Sanskrit 67 is the young/old verse), so the card names Sinh.

final.prop_idea:
B0, silent, about 2 s, started mid-action (film about 5 s; the editor keeps the best 2 s): on his mat in dim shala light he already holds his phone in selfie mode like a mirror, squinting. He pushes his reading glasses on and leans in at the lines by his eyes (and the grey at his temple, but only if he really has grey), then looks at the lens over the glasses: 'Eh? You never check?' The glasses stay ON for the whole act as the 'expert' costume. B6: 1 s silent, he takes them off and folds them, so sound-off viewers see the switch from act to truth. B9: he turns the phone face down (the B0 mirror, closing the hook's loop), puts the folded glasses on it ('not from reading') and steps onto the mat ('only from practice'). Props: mat, phone, reading glasses only; a cup of tea on the floor is optional and stays untouched.
EDIT CUE SHEET: (1) Header pill, whole video: '[SERIES: Boonchu to pick]' until he answers. (2) Corner tag from 0:00 until the glasses fold (about 0:22): 'GAME: old-book promises. True or false? Answers at the end.' On the fold it changes to 'GAME OVER. All 3: no proof.' (3) Cards (house SVG style, pop in) as written in each beat's on-screen line. B8: reveal the list one line at a time as he says it, the three crosses first, then clear them and show the tick alone, so no frame holds more than 12 words. B9: 'Start with one second. Learn inversions with a teacher.' on the gold line, then the 1.67 card on the last line. (4) 1.3x zoom punch for about 1 s on 'gone', 'sixteen', 'poison', 'None of this is mine', 'practice'; SFX at 40%, starting 0.4 s after each of those words. (5) Weight Shift captions (lowercase Montserrat, the line being said turns bold) with big emoji. (6) Keep the 2 s B0 silence and the 1 s silent fold at B6; cut other pauses after his 1.2x speed-up. (7) No image of any god (no Shiva, no kalakuta). No student on screen during B2 or 'old man'. Mayurasana or Sirsasana B-roll only after the glasses come off (B7 to B9), never during a promise. No generated images needed (the props carry it). (8) Final video to Boonchu's Google Drive, never the repo.
final.caption:
Hidden Stories of Ashtanga: the old book that promised to make you young.
Years on the mat, and a quiet hope that it keeps you young.
A 15th-century yoga book makes 3 big promises. No study has tested the grey hair or the poison promise, and nobody turns sixteen. What holds: old muscle still answers training (Mayo Clinic 2017, ages 65 to 80, not a yoga study), and success comes from practice, not reading. Learn inversions step by step, with a teacher. Neck injury, high blood pressure or eye pressure problems? Ask your doctor first. Mayurasana: not in pregnancy, with a hernia or on a full stomach.
New students: buy 1, get 1 free on 1, 2 or 3 months, till 11 Nov. Comment aybkk
Aybkk.net #aybkk #ashtanga #ashtangabangkok #hiddenstoriesofashtanga #mayurasana #boonchutanti
ask_boonchu: Toolkit pick (now at the top): Interrupt Opener (silent phone-mirror check) + the speech's beat skeleton, with Two-Voice Deadpan at the glasses-off switch and Myth-Kill in B8. OK, or do you want another tool?
Do you have grey hair? If yes, B0 can show you checking it. If not, B0 shows only the lines by your eyes. B2 stays the same either way, because it is the book's promise, not yours.

'Me too': B8 now says only 'All three? ... I wish.' ('I wish' echoes your letter P.S.: 'I wish we could say we are growing young.') Did you really once believe all three promises? Only if yes, 'Me too' goes back before 'I wish', and 'Same here.' goes back in caption line 2.
In your early years, did you ever believe one of these three promises? If yes, tell Plato the true line and it can go into B8. Never claim it if it didn't happen.
Can you hold Mayurasana and Sirsasana for B-roll? Plato's advice: show them only after the glasses come off (B7 to B9), never during the promises, so no clip ever pairs a promise with the asana.

Series label: the header says '[SERIES: Boonchu to pick]' until you answer. Keep it under Hidden Stories of Ashtanga (no Ep. number until filmed), or start a small side series ('Old book promises')? If side series: caption line 1 becomes 'Old book promises: how many did you believe?' and #hiddenstoriesofashtanga is dropped. Note: this Reel has no myth story and teaches no asana; purists have noticed that before ('the teachers never needed myths').

Are you OK with the corner tag 'GAME: old-book promises. True or false? Answers at the end.' on every frame from 0:00 until the glasses come off (about 0:22), then 'GAME OVER. All 3: no proof.'? Every promise card credits the old book and ends in '?'. It is the main safety net if someone clips the first 20 seconds.
Delivery: say the promises like a warm, sincere believer, not like a salesman you are making fun of. Then, after the 1 s silent fold, switch to your normal voice at B6. Does that feel natural to you?

B9 'With a teacher. That part... we still do.' says that at AYBKK inversions are learned step by step, with a teacher. Is that how you teach them? If not, cut the line, and the Reel becomes habit #2 only.
risks: PURIST VERDICT (honest): NOT fully safe for strict purists. It is safe for most 5 to 20 year practitioners if it is delivered with respect. Why it is not purist-safe: (1) a respected yoga text plays the 'promiser' in a game frame, and some will hear 'the book's promises are false' as disrespect; (2) Guruji quotes the Hatha Yoga Pradipika in Yoga Mala (e.g. 1.66 on age), so some will feel we undercut his sources; (3) many read '16' and 'poison' as pictures of vitality or of the mind, so fact-checking them word for word can look shallow to them. Built-in mitigations: the cards say 'promises' and credit the 'old book', never 'lies' or 'myths'; Shiva and kalakuta stay out; Boonchu never says 'the book is wrong'; the moral aims at the promise and at Boonchu ('Even when I say it'), never at the book or Svatmarama; B9 praises the book ('the book has gold too') and ends on its own line. For a more purist-proof cut: in B6 say 'None of this is mine. It's from a book I respect, 500 years old.'

CLIP RISK: for about 21 s (B1 to B4) Boonchu says false things with full confidence. Mitigations: (a) corner tag 'GAME: old-book promises. True or false? Answers at the end.' on every frame from 0:00 until the glasses fold; (b) every promise card starts 'GAME n/3 · Old book:' and ends with '?', so a silent clip reads as a quiz about an old book, not as advice; (c) only low-harm promises; cut on purpose: 'destroys all diseases', 'conquers death', 'two hours daily', 'digests food taken in excess', 'Head on the floor. Feet to the sky.' (a how-to), 'Big mistake' (a push to do Mayurasana) and the B5 'secret' (a conspiracy frame); (d) glasses off and 'GAME OVER. All 3: no proof.' at about 0:22 to 0:23; the spoken truths start at about 0:34, each said plainly in B8.

INVERSION SAFETY: someone could clip B2 and hold Sirsasana longer for their hair. Mitigations: B2 no longer says how to go upside down; the B2 card credits the old book and asks 'True?'; 'With a teacher' is spoken in B9, shown on the B9 card ('Start with one second. Learn inversions with a teacher.') and in the caption with the neck, blood pressure and eye pressure line. Never show a student upside down during B2. Never suggest holding longer for looks.

B4 MAYURASANA: 'Big mistake' is gone, but a clip of B4 alone still says the peacock kills poison. The net is the corner tag, the '?' card, B8 'Keep away from poison' and the caption line (not in pregnancy, with a hernia or on a full stomach). The 'Go to hospital' line was cut as a punchline; if Boonchu wants a stronger net, the checked line is 'real poisoning needs emergency care' (verified.json, peacock safety).
B3 'Breath and bandha... like sixteen again' never says 'hold your breath', so a clip does not teach breath retention. Keep it that way in the take.

EVIDENCE WORDING: 'No study test it' is a claim that something is missing. One verifier could only hedge it ('we found no study'). Never upgrade it to 'proven false'. Never say 'grey hair: no study' (grey hair has been studied: Rosenberg et al., eLife 2021); always 'upside down for grey hair'.
